title: Saved by the Bell Cast Then and Now (2026 Update): Where Are They Today?
excerpt: Discover where the Saved by the Bell cast is today in 2026. From Dustin Diamond's tribute to Zack Morris and Kelly Kapowski — get the complete Bayside update.
content:
For every American kid who grew up in the early 1990s, Saturday mornings did not truly begin until the high-energy electric guitar riffs and ringing school bell of NBC’s *Saved by the Bell* blasted through the living room CRT television. Debuting under its definitive title in 1989 after evolving from the short-lived Disney Channel series *Good Morning, Miss Bliss*, executive producer Peter Engel created a candy-colored, optimistic high school utopia at Palisades’ fictional Bayside High. 

With oversized neon locker hallways, the Max burger diner, cell phones the size of shoeboxes, and fourth-wall-breaking *“Time Out!”* freeze-frames, *Saved by the Bell* was a Saturday morning phenomenon that captured the imaginations of over 10 million weekly teen viewers across the globe.

In this comprehensive 2026 retrospective, we journey back to the halls of Bayside High to explore the triumphs, heartbreaks, and exact 2026 whereabouts of Zack, Kelly, Slater, Jessie, Lisa, and Screech.

![Saved by the Bell cast 1989](/images/articles/saved-by-the-bell-cast-1989.jpg)

---

## The Bayside High Crew — Then and Now

### Mark-Paul Gosselaar (Zack Morris)
With his peroxide-blonde hair, oversized brick cell phone, and undeniable charm, Zack Morris was the ultimate high school schemer who could talk his way out of detention with Principal Belding and freeze live television action with a snap of his fingers. Naturally brunette, Gosselaar had his hair chemically bleached every two weeks for five straight years to maintain Zack’s golden California aesthetic.

Proving his skeptics wrong, Gosselaar engineered one of the most successful transitions from teen idol to respected dramatic actor in Hollywood history. He spent four seasons playing Detective John Clark Jr. on ABC’s gritty police procedural *NYPD Blue*, starred in TNT’s legal dramedy *Franklin & Bash*, and currently stars in NBC’s hit missing-persons thriller *Found*. In the 2020 Peacock reboot, Gosselaar reprised Zack Morris as the self-absorbed Governor of California, holding an estimated net worth of $9 million.

![Mark-Paul Gosselaar as Zack Morris 1989](/images/articles/mark-paul-gosselaar-zack-1989.jpg)

### Lark Voorhies (Lisa Turtle)
Lark Voorhies brought elegance, sharp wit, and high fashion to Lisa Turtle, Bayside's wealthy fashionista who relentlessly shut down Screech's corny advances while remaining a fiercely loyal friend to Kelly and Jessie. Voorhies won two Young Artist Awards for her magnetic performance.

Following *Saved by the Bell*, Voorhies starred in daytime soap operas *Days of Our Lives* and *The Bold and the Beautiful*. In recent years, Voorhies stepped away from the spotlight to manage schizoaffective disorder, supported by her family. After fans passionately campaigned for her return, Voorhies made a radiant, celebrated guest appearance in the Peacock revival series as a world-famous fashion designer, holding an estimated net worth of $500,000.

![Lark Voorhies as Screech 2025](/images/articles/lark-voorhies-scrreech-2025.jpg)

### Dustin Diamond (Screech Powers) — 1977-2021
No character was more synonymous with *Saved by the Bell* than Samuel “Screech” Powers, portrayed with rubber-faced physical hilarity by child prodigy Dustin Diamond. Cast when he was just eleven years old—three years younger than his co-stars—Diamond brought Screech to life through wild shirts, his robot companion Kevin, and his unrequited love for Lisa Turtle. Remarkably, Diamond was the only original cast member to appear in every single incarnation of the franchise, tallying over 240 episodes.

Tragically, in January 2021, Diamond was diagnosed with Stage 4 small-cell lung carcinoma that had rapidly metastasized. Just three weeks later, on February 1, 2021, Dustin Diamond passed away at the age of 44. Co-stars Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez remembered him as a true comedic genius whose goofy warmth brightened millions of childhoods. When the Peacock sequel series aired its second season, the cast dedicated a tearful memorial episode to Screech at The Max.

![Dustin Diamond as Screech 2020](/images/articles/dustin-diamond-scrreech-2020.jpg)

### Tiffani Thiessen (Kelly Kapowski)
As head cheerleader, volleyball captain, and homecoming queen Kelly Kapowski, Tiffani Thiessen was the quintessential 1990s dream crush for an entire generation. From her high-waisted acid-washed jeans to her off-the-shoulder Bayside sweatshirts, Thiessen set nationwide fashion trends.

Immediately after *Saved by the Bell* wrapped, Thiessen joined FOX’s primetime juggernaut *Beverly Hills, 90210* as scheming vixen Valerie Malone. She went on to star in USA Network’s *White Collar* for six seasons. Over the past decade, Thiessen has channeled her passion for culinary entertaining into the Cooking Channel, hosting *Dinner at Tiffani’s* and authoring bestselling cookbooks *Pull Up a Chair* and *Here We Go Again*, holding a net worth of $10 million.

![Tiffani Thiessen as Kelly Kapowski 2025](/images/articles/tiffani-thiessen-kelly-2025.jpg)

### Mario Lopez (A.C. Slater)
Albert Clifford “A.C.” Slater strutted into Bayside High in his tight wrestling singlets and backwards caps, calling Zack *“Preppy”* and immediately engaging in an epic battle for Kelly Kapowski’s heart before becoming Zack’s truest brother. 

Today, Mario Lopez is one of the most recognizable, prolific television hosts in American broadcasting. After finishing as runner-up on *Dancing with the Stars* in 2006, Lopez cemented his broadcast career hosting *Extra*, *The X Factor*, and *Access Hollywood*. An avid Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt and devoted father of three with wife Courtney Mazza, Lopez reprised Slater in the Peacock reboot as Bayside's athletic director, holding an estimated net worth of $35 million.

![Mario Lopez as A.C. Slater 2025](/images/articles/mario-lopez-slater-2025.jpg)

### Elizabeth Berkley (Jessie Spano)
As high-achieving feminist valedictorian Jessica “Jessie” Spano, Elizabeth Berkley brought passionate social consciousness to Saturday mornings. Her performance in the legendary 1990 episode where an over-caffeinated Jessie collapses singing *“I’m So Excited!”* remains one of the most viral scenes in youth television history.

Following the series, Berkley starred in Paul Verhoeven’s cult classic *Showgirls*, later reclaimed as a camp masterpiece, and earned widespread critical acclaim on Broadway. Berkley founded *Ask-Elizabeth*, an acclaimed nationwide adolescent self-esteem program and bestselling book that has empowered hundreds of thousands of teenage girls across American schools. She returned as an executive producer and star of the 2020 *Saved by the Bell* revival, holding an estimated net worth of $6 million.

![Elizabeth Berkley as Jessie Spano 2025](/images/articles/elizabeth-berkley-jessie-2025.jpg)

### Guest Stars & Early Appearances
Before becoming household names, numerous young actors made memorable early appearances at Bayside High. Future *Boy Meets World* lead Ben Savage appeared as young student Bobby Singer, while stars like Tori Spelling (Violet Bickerstaff) and Soleil Moon Frye made iconic guest stops at The Max.

![Ben Savage as Bobby Singer 2025](/images/articles/ben-savage-bobby-2025.jpg)

---

## Supporting Cast

### Dennis Haskins (Principal Richard Belding)
No discussion of Bayside High is complete without Dennis Haskins’ unforgettable portrayal of Principal Richard Belding. Haskins brought genuine warmth and comic exasperation to Belding’s constant battle to keep Zack Morris from running unauthorized casino operations and radio stations in the locker rooms. In 2026, Haskins remains a beloved fixture at 90s fan conventions, frequently visiting college campuses to lead alumni in the iconic Bayside school fight song.

![Saved by the Bell cast reunion 2020](/images/articles/saved-by-the-bell-reunion-2020.jpg)

---

## The 2020 Peacock Reboot
In November 2020, NBC’s streaming platform Peacock premiered a critically acclaimed, satirical revival of *Saved by the Bell* developed by Emmy-winning writer Tracey Wigfield. The reboot ingeniously commented on privilege, modern education, and 90s television tropes while reuniting Zack, Kelly, Slater, Jessie, and Lisa. The series ran for two celebrated seasons, earning a GLAAD Media Award before concluding in 2022.

![Saved by the Bell catchphrase Let take five](/images/articles/saved-by-the-bell-lets-take-five.jpg)

---

---

## The Origins: Good Morning, Miss Bliss and the Transition to Bayside

Long before the sun-drenched halls of Palisades' Bayside High School entered television lore, the series actually began in Indianapolis, Indiana! In 1988, NBC and Disney Channel produced an experimental comedy titled *Good Morning, Miss Bliss*, centered on veteran actress Hayley Mills playing a devoted middle school teacher.

While the original concept struggled in the ratings, NBC executive Brandon Tartikoff spotted something extraordinary in the young supporting cast: a charismatic, mischievous 14-year-old named Mark-Paul Gosselaar, a nerdy 11-year-old prodigy named Dustin Diamond, and a stylish fashionista named Lark Voorhies. Tartikoff made the bold executive decision to fire the adult leads, move the setting across the country to Southern California, rename the school Bayside High, and retool the concept around teenage romance and friendship.

Producer Peter Engel was brought in to helm the newly rechristened *Saved by the Bell*. Engel added Mario Lopez as athletic wrestler A.C. Slater, Tiffani Thiessen as quintessential cheerleader Kelly Kapowski, and Elizabeth Berkley as passionate feminist Jessie Spano. The combination ignited overnight lightning. When the revamped series premiered on NBC Saturday mornings in August 1989, it captured the imaginations of over 10 million weekly teen viewers across the globe.

---

## The Television Movies & The College Years

As the characters graduated from Bayside High, NBC was reluctant to let go of its golden goose. In 1992, the network produced *Saved by the Bell: Hawaiian Style*, where the gang flew to Honolulu to help Kelly's grandfather save his hideaway resort from greedy developers. 

Following high school graduation, NBC took a high-stakes gamble by moving Zack, Slater, and Screech into a primetime spin-off titled *Saved by the Bell: The College Years* in 1993, set at fictional Cal U alongside Kelly Kapowski and Bob Golic as resident advisor Mike Rogers. While the primetime experiment lasted only a single 19-episode season against titans like *Full House*, it culminated in the two-hour television movie *Saved by the Bell: Wedding in Las Vegas* in 1994, where high school sweethearts Zack Morris and Kelly Kapowski finally tied the knot in front of millions of emotional viewers.

![Saved by the Bell reunion 2020](/images/articles/saved-by-the-bell-reunion-2020.jpg)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What happened to Dustin Diamond?
Dustin Diamond passed away on February 1, 2021, at age 44 from Stage 4 small-cell lung carcinoma, just three weeks after being diagnosed. His castmates paid emotional tribute to his legacy, and the 2020 revival dedicated a special episode in his honor.

### Is Mark-Paul Gosselaar still acting?
Yes, Mark-Paul Gosselaar is one of the most prolific dramatic actors on television, currently starring as Sir on NBC’s hit drama series *Found* following acclaimed roles on *NYPD Blue*, *Pitch*, and *Franklin & Bash*.

### What is Tiffani Thiessen doing now?
Tiffani Thiessen is a successful culinary personality, cookbook author (*Pull Up a Chair*, *Here We Go Again*), and host of MTV’s comedy clip series *Deliciousness*.

Lark Voorhies lives in Southern California, authoring books and advocating for mental health awareness. She made a celebrated return to acting in the 2020 *Saved by the Bell* revival.

Mario Lopez hosts *Access Hollywood*, produces television holiday movies, and is an active Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu competitor and fitness author.

title: Full House Cast Then and Now (2026 Update): Where Are They Today?
excerpt: Discover where the Full House cast is today in 2026. From Bob Saget's legacy to the Olsen twins' fashion empire — get the complete then and now update.
content:
Every Friday night between 1987 and 1995, millions of American families gathered around their television sets, dialed into ABC’s legendary TGIF lineup, and were greeted by the sunny, cheerful chimes of Jesse Frederick singing *“Everywhere You Look.”* Debuting on September 22, 1987, *Full House* was not merely a top-ten television sitcom; it was the definitive emotional anchor of 1990s childhood. The colorful Victorian row home on San Francisco’s Girard Street represented the ultimate sanctuary—a place where a grieving widowed father, an Elvis-loving rock-and-roll brother-in-law, and an eccentric cartoon-voice comic could join forces to raise three spirited young girls.

Generations of viewers grew up learning life lessons alongside D.J., Stephanie, and baby Michelle. Yet behind the bright pastel colors, pristine San Francisco backdrops, and heartwarming acoustic guitar hug-cues, the real lives of the cast members were fraught with shocking off-screen struggles, intense creative battles, Hollywood scandals, and heartbreaking grief. 

In this comprehensive 2026 retrospective, we examine the complete journey of the Tanner family—honoring the beloved stars we have lost, exploring the surprising career pivots of its child stars, and detailing exactly where the entire cast of *Full House* stands today.

![Full House cast 1987 Danny Tanner family](/images/articles/full-house-cast-1987.jpg)

---

## The Tanner Family — Then and Now

### Bob Saget (Danny Tanner) — 1956-2022
For eight seasons, Bob Saget portrayed Danny Tanner, the meticulously clean, affectionate morning host of *Wake Up, San Francisco*. Danny was the moral center of the show, famous for his dust-buster routines, hugging rituals, and sincere fatherly chats. Outside of the G-rated soundstage, however, Saget was an uncompromising, boundary-pushing stand-up comedian whose filthy club routines were legendary among Hollywood peers. Yet despite his adult comedic persona, Saget harbored deep maternal tenderness for his TV daughters, maintaining a paternal guardian role for Mary-Kate, Ashley, Candace, and Jodie throughout their adult lives.

Tragically, on January 9, 2022, the entertainment world was shattered when Bob Saget was found deceased in his room at the Ritz-Carlton in Orlando, Florida, following a celebrated two-hour stand-up comedy performance. An autopsy determined his death was the result of blunt head trauma, likely from an accidental, unwitnessed fall backward. He was 65 years old. 

Saget’s sudden passing triggered an unprecedented outpouring of worldwide grief. Co-stars John Stamos and Dave Coulier served as pallbearers, and the surviving cast released a heartbreaking joint statement declaring: *“Bob was our brother, our father, and our friend. We will miss him forever.”* In 2026, Saget’s legacy lives on through the Scleroderma Research Foundation—a charity he passionately championed for thirty years. His estate was valued at an estimated $50 million at the time of his passing.

![Bob Saget as Danny Tanner 1987](/images/articles/bob-saget-danny-tanner-1987.jpg)

### John Stamos (Uncle Jesse)
With his jet-black mullet, leather motorcycle jackets, Beach Boys obsession, and smooth catchphrase *“Have mercy!”*, John Stamos transformed Uncle Jesse into the definitive television heartthrob of the 1990s. Behind the camera, Stamos was the linchpin who spearheaded the show's 2016 Netflix revival, *Fuller House*, serving as an executive producer and recurring guest star.

In October 2023, Stamos released his deeply vulnerable, bestselling memoir, *If You Would Have Told Me*, where he laid bare his decades-long sobriety journey, his emotional confrontation with past trauma, and the devastating grief of losing his best friend Bob Saget. Now happily married to actress Caitlin McHugh and embracing late-in-life fatherhood with his son Billy, Stamos remains remarkably youthful. In 2026, he continues to perform live on tour with The Beach Boys, guest stars on critically acclaimed television dramas, and holds an estimated net worth of $25 million.

![John Stamos as Uncle Jesse 2025](/images/articles/john-stamos-uncle-jesse-2025.jpg)

### Candace Cameron Bure (D.J. Tanner)
As the responsible, boy-crazy eldest daughter D.J. Tanner, Candace Cameron Bure grew up directly in front of the television camera from ages 10 to 18. Her character navigated realistic adolescent trials, from body image insecurities to obtaining a driver’s license and surviving high school heartbreak.

In 1996, at age 20, Candace married Russian NHL hockey superstar Valeri Bure—after being introduced at a charity hockey match by co-star Dave Coulier! Over the past two decades, Bure transformed herself into a formidable business powerhouse, headlining over two dozen holiday films for Hallmark Channel before transitioning to Great American Family in 2022 as an executive producer and Chief Creative Officer. As mother to three adult children and author of multiple bestselling books, Candace holds an estimated net worth of $14 million in 2026.

![Candace Cameron Bure 2025 with family](/images/articles/candace-cameron-bure-family-2025.jpg)

### Jodie Sweetin (Stephanie Tanner)
Jodie Sweetin’s portrayal of middle child Stephanie Tanner provided *Full House* with some of its greatest punchlines (*“How rude!”*), dynamic dance routines, and gut-wrenching dramatic moments.

Following the sitcom’s cancellation, Sweetin faced a harrowing, well-documented battle with substance abuse throughout her late teens and twenties. In her brutally honest 2009 autobiography, *unSweetined*, Sweetin chronicled her journey through addiction, recovery, and rehabilitation. Having maintained rigorous sobriety for well over a decade, Sweetin has become an outspoken public advocate for addiction recovery, mental health awareness, and LGBTQ+ equality. Married to clinical social worker Mescal Wasilewski, Sweetin continues to work as a television host, podcast creator, and reality TV competitor, holding an estimated net worth of $2 million.

![Jodie Sweetin 2025 Summer House](/images/articles/jodie-sweetin-stephanie-2025.jpg)

### Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen (Michelle Tanner)
Cast at just nine months old, Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen alternated playing baby Michelle Tanner so the production could comply with strict California child labor laws. By the time Michelle was uttering catchphrases like *“You got it, dude!”* and *“No way, José!”*, the twins had evolved into a multi-million-dollar empire under their Dualstar production company.

After starring in their final joint film *New York Minute* in 2004, the Olsen twins walked away from Hollywood acting forever. Enrolling at NYU, they channeled their acute creative discipline into luxury fashion, establishing their iconic couture label **The Row** in 2006. Today, The Row is an internationally lauded titan of quiet luxury with multi-billion-dollar private valuations, and both sisters are decorated multiple-time CFDA Fashion Award winners. With a combined net worth exceeding $500 million, they maintain quiet, deeply private personal lives in New York City.

![Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen 2025 fashion](/images/articles/olsen-twins-fashion-2025.jpg)

---

## Supporting Cast — Then and Now

### Dave Coulier (Joey Gladstone)
As Joey Gladstone, Dave Coulier brought manic cartoon impressions, ventriloquist puppet Mr. Woodchuck, and his unforgettable signature scissor gesture *“Cut. It. Out.”* into the living rooms of over 20 million weekly viewers. Coulier met Bob Saget on the Detroit comedy circuit when he was just an 18-year-old aspiring comic, forming a lifelong brotherhood.

In November 2024, Coulier shared shocking personal news that resonated across the global nostalgia community: he was diagnosed with Stage 3 non-Hodgkin lymphoma, an aggressive form of blood cancer. Supported by his wife Melissa Bring and lifelong brother John Stamos—who famously wore a bald cap to publicly stand in solidarity with Coulier during his chemotherapy treatments—Coulier has tackled his diagnosis with inspiring humor and bravery. Hosting his popular podcast *Full House Rewind*, Coulier holds an estimated net worth of $5 million.

![Dave Coulier as Joey Gladstone 2025](/images/articles/dave-coulier-joey-2025.jpg)

### Lori Loughlin (Rebecca Donaldson)
Introduced in Season 2 as Danny’s charming co-anchor on *Wake Up, San Francisco*, Lori Loughlin’s character Rebecca Donaldson was initially slated for a brief six-episode arc. However, her radiant screen presence and undeniable romantic chemistry with John Stamos captivated producers, transforming Aunt Becky into an indispensable series regular and Jesse’s wife.

Loughlin’s squeaky-clean image suffered a catastrophic blow in 2019 during the nationwide college admissions bribery scandal. After serving a two-month federal prison sentence in late 2020 and completing 100 hours of community service, Loughlin steadily rebuilt her career. By 2026, she has returned to television prominence as a leading romantic lead on the Great American Family network, holding an estimated joint net worth of $70 million with husband Mossimo Giannulli.

![Lori Loughlin as Gina Castaneda 2025](/images/articles/lori-loughlin-gina-2025.jpg)

### Andrea Barber (Kimmy Gibbler)
No episode of *Full House* was complete without Kimmy Gibbler barging through the Tanner back door unannounced, sporting mismatched neon leggings and smelly footwear. Andrea Barber’s comedic timing as D.J.’s loud, loyal, and unapologetic best friend provided the series with some of its funniest moments.

When *Full House* wrapped in 1995, Barber retired from show business at age 18. She earned a Master’s degree in Women’s Studies from the University of York in England and worked in college administration. In 2016, Barber enthusiastically stepped back into Kimmy Gibbler’s flamboyant wardrobe for all five seasons of *Fuller House*. Today, Barber is an accomplished author (*Full Circle*), marathon runner, and beloved convention headliner with an estimated net worth of $2 million.

![Full House cast reunion 2014](/images/articles/full-house-cast-reunion-2014.jpg)

---

## Full House vs Fuller House

### The Netflix Revival Details
In February 2016, Netflix premiered *Fuller House*, a sequel series created by original creator Jeff Franklin that inverted the classic premise: a recently widowed D.J. Tanner-Fuller moves back into her childhood home, joined by sister Stephanie and best friend Kimmy to help raise D.J.’s three young sons. The reboot shattered viewership records for Netflix, running for five seasons (75 episodes) and earning multiple People's Choice and Kids' Choice Awards before concluding with a triple wedding in 2020.

### Why It Didn't Feel the Same
While *Fuller House* delivered powerful nostalgia, many purist fans noted that it lacked the authentic, grounded heart of the original 1990s run. Without Bob Saget as a full-time resident patriarch and with the complete absence of Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen's Michelle Tanner, the show relied heavily on self-referential catchphrases and exaggerated slapstick. Furthermore, the modern HD multi-camera aesthetic felt overly bright compared to the warm, cozy CRT glow that defined Friday nights in the 1990s.

![Full House Zack Morris catchphrase Let take five](/images/articles/full-house-let-take-five.jpg)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What happened to Bob Saget?
Bob Saget passed away on January 9, 2022, in his hotel room at the Ritz-Carlton in Orlando, Florida, following a celebrated stand-up comedy performance. An autopsy determined his death was caused by accidental blunt head trauma, most likely from slipping backward and striking the back of his head before going to sleep, unaware of the severity of the injury.

### Where are Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen now?
Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen retired from acting in 2004 to build their luxury fashion house, *The Row*, which has become an internationally acclaimed multi-billion-dollar brand. They live private, quiet lives in New York City, designing couture apparel and choosing to preserve Michelle Tanner's childhood innocence away from Hollywood cameras.

### Why didn't Lori Loughlin return for Fuller House's final season?
Lori Loughlin was written out of the fifth and final season of *Fuller House* in 2019 due to her legal involvement in the nationwide college admissions bribery scandal. The production addressed Aunt Becky's absence by explaining she was out of town in Nebraska visiting her mother.

### Is John Stamos still active in entertainment?
Yes, John Stamos remains extraordinarily active in entertainment. In addition to touring live worldwide with The Beach Boys as a guest drummer and guitarist, Stamos released his bestselling memoir *If You Would Have Told Me* in 2023 and regularly guest stars on prime-time television dramas.

### What is Candace Cameron Bure doing now?
Candace Cameron Bure serves as the Chief Creative Officer and executive producer at Great American Family, starring in numerous holiday feature films and family dramas. She is also a prolific author of children's and lifestyle books and oversees her own lifestyle brand.

### Did the Full House cast stay friends?
Yes! The cast of *Full House* is universally recognized as having one of the closest, most enduring real-life friendships in television history. John Stamos, Dave Coulier, and Bob Saget considered each other brothers, and the entire cast regularly gathers for weddings, charity benefits, podcasts, and fan conventions in 2026.

---

## Conclusion

*Full House* was more than just a sitcom; it was a warm, welcoming blanket for an entire generation of 1990s kids who found comfort in Danny's advice, Jesse's music, and Joey's silly voices. While time has brought heartbreaking loss and real-world trials to the cast, their unbreakable bond continues to inspire millions of fans across the globe.

title: The Heartbreaking True Story Behind Brenda and Dylan: How Luke Perry and Shannen Doherty’s Off-Screen Bond Outlasted Beverly Hills, 90210
excerpt: Discover the untold true story of Brenda Walsh and Dylan McKay, Shannen Doherty’s controversial departure, Luke Perry’s secret loyalty, and their enduring bond.
content:
In the autumn of 1990, Fox took a daring gamble on an hour-long primetime teen soap opera created by Darren Star and executive produced by Aaron Spelling. While *Beverly Hills, 90210* initially debuted to modest ratings, the electric on-screen chemistry between midwestern transplant **Brenda Walsh (Shannen Doherty)** and brooding, James Dean-inspired rebel **Dylan McKay (Luke Perry)** ignited an unprecedented pop-culture phenomenon.

Their passionate, turbulent romance didn't merely dominate 90s magazine covers—it fundamentally reshaped teenage drama on television. Yet behind the sun-drenched glamour of West Beverly High and the Peach Pit, the real-life dynamic between Doherty and Perry was rooted in something far deeper than Hollywood romance: a fierce, protective lifelong loyalty that outlasted tabloid scandals, backstage dismissals, and profound personal tragedies.

---

## The Electric Spark That Saved the Series

When Luke Perry first auditioned for the role of Dylan McKay, Fox network executives were intensely skeptical. In fact, network brass originally refused to grant Perry full cast status, viewing Dylan merely as a fleeting, two-episode bad-boy guest star.

However, the moment Perry stepped onto the soundstage opposite Shannen Doherty, the creative atmosphere shifted completely. Aaron Spelling instantly recognized the raw, electric tension between the vulnerable Minnesota newcomer and the wealthy, neglected loner. Spelling was so convinced of their magic that he personally funded Perry’s salary out of his own pocket until Fox relented and signed him as a series regular.

For eight seasons and 204 episodes between 1991 and 1999, ABC's *Home Improvement* was one of the most beloved sitcoms in American television history. Millions of families gathered every Tuesday night to watch Tim "The Tool Man" Taylor fumble through DIY projects, grunt over horsepower, and dispense well-meaning but flawed marital advice.

Yet, of all the comedy running gags in the series, none captured pop-culture imagination quite like Tim's eccentric, hyper-wise backyard neighbor: **Wilson W. Wilson Jr., PhD**, portrayed brilliantly by veteran character actor **Earl Hindman**.

In every single episode, Wilson leaned over the cedar fence to offer profound philosophical quotes, historical folklore, and gentle wisdom to solve Tim's dilemmas. But viewers never saw his mouth or chin. Whether hidden behind the fence pickets, a potted fern, a towering stack of books, a baseball glove, or a BBQ grill, Wilsonâ€™s lower face was strictly concealed.

So, **why was Wilson's face never shown on Home Improvement?** Here is the true, heartwarming childhood story behind televisionâ€™s greatest running mystery, the tragic fate of Earl Hindman, and where the cast is today.

---

## The Real Childhood Inspiration Behind Wilson's Fence

The genius behind Wilson's hidden face wasn't created by Hollywood network executives or focus groupsâ€”it was directly inspired by **Tim Allen's real-life childhood memories**.

Growing up in suburban Colorado, a young Tim Allen was simply too short to see over his family's high wooden backyard fence. Whenever the elderly neighbor in the adjacent yard was tending his garden, Tim could only see the manâ€™s eyes and the top of his hat. Despite never actually seeing the neighbor's face, the man regularly spoke with young Tim, offering neighborly wisdom, life advice, and grandfatherly perspectives.

When developing *Home Improvement* alongside creators Matt Williams, Carmen Finestra, and David McFadzean, Allen pitched the idea of turning his childhood perspective into a permanent visual gag. To young children, adults often seem like disembodied voices of wisdom leaning over barriers. The creators loved the concept, and Wilson W. Wilson Jr. was born.

---

## How Earl Hindman Committed to the Gag (Even Off-Camera)

While lesser actors might have fought to have their full faces showcased on primetime television, **Earl Hindman embraced the mystery with total artistic devotion**.

A seasoned stage actor with decades of experience on Broadway and in classic daytime drama (*Ryan's Hope*), Hindman recognized that the mystery of Wilson was what made the character unforgettable. He meticulously coordinated every camera angle, rehearsing props so that every mug sip, newspaper fold, or birdfeeder adjustment perfectly obscured his mouth and chin down to the millimeter.

Hindman took the commitment even further: **during live studio audience curtain calls after filming, he still refused to reveal his face!** While the rest of the cast took their bows, Hindman would walk out holding a small miniature fence prop on a stick in front of his face, delighting the studio audience while keeping the legendary illusion 100% alive.

---

## Did Home Improvement Ever Actually Show Wilson's Face?

Throughout the entire eight-season run, Wilson's lower face was never revealed during an actual storyline episode. 

However, during the emotional **series finale curtain call on May 25, 1999**, Earl Hindman finally gave fans the payoff they had anticipated for nearly a decade. As the cast took their final bow following the emotional series finale, Hindman walked out onto the Taylor family set, smiling warmly, and lowered the prop fence to reveal his complete face to a thunderous standing ovation from the cast and crowd.

## The Heartbreaking Passing of Earl Hindman (1942â€“2003)

Tragically, just four years after *Home Improvement* concluded its historic run, the entertainment community lost its favorite neighbor.

Earl Hindman, a longtime heavy smoker, was diagnosed with lung cancer in 2003. Despite undergoing treatment at Stamford Hospital in Connecticut, he passed away on **December 29, 2003, at the age of 61**. 

His co-stars were devastated. Tim Allen paid emotional tribute to Hindman, praising him not only as an exceptional classical actor, but as a warm, generous soul who truly was as kind, cultured, and wise in real life as the character he immortalized on television.

In *Home Improvement* lore, Wilson's full formal name was Wilson Wilson Wilson Jr.â€”his middle name was literally "Wilson," making him Wilson cubed!

content:
On September 17, 1991, ABC launched a comedy based on the stand-up routines of comedian Tim Allen centered around male communication, power tools, and high-octane DIY disasters. For eight seasons and 204 episodes, *Home Improvement* was one of the most dominant ratings behemoths in television history, routinely attracting over 30 million weekly American viewers and briefly holding the #1 spot on television ahead of *Seinfeld*.

The suburban garage of Tim “The Toolman” Taylor, his long-suffering intellectual wife Jill (Patricia Richardson), their three rambunctious sons (Brad, Randy, and Mark), flannel-clad co-host Al Borland (Richard Karn), and wise backyard neighbor Wilson (Earl Hindman) became a staple of American family life.

Yet beneath the signature ape grunts (*“Argh, argh, argh!”*) and exploding dishwashers, the cast experienced immense real-world pressures—from teen idol hysteria and tragic losses to surprising Hollywood retirements. In this 2026 retrospective, we check in on the entire Taylor household.

![Home Improvement Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/home-improvement-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## Tim Allen (Tim ‘The Toolman’ Taylor) — “More Power!”
Tim Allen brought frantic energy, masculine self-parody, and genuine domestic love to Tim Taylor, the accident-prone host of *Tool Time*. In November 1994, Allen accomplished an unprecedented Hollywood trifecta never achieved before or since: he had the #1 television show in America (*Home Improvement*), the #1 box office film in America (*The Santa Clause*), and the #1 *New York Times* bestselling book (*Don't Stand Too Close to a Naked Man*) all in the exact same week!

Allen achieved cinematic immortality as the voice of Space Ranger Buzz Lightyear in Disney/Pixar’s groundbreaking *Toy Story* franchise. He led ABC/FOX’s *Last Man Standing* for nine successful seasons, starred in Disney+’s *The Santa Clauses*, and in 2025 returned to multi-cam sitcoms headlining ABC's *Shifting Gears* alongside Kat Dennings. Today in 2026, Allen remains one of television's most durable and beloved comedic superstars.

![Tim Allen Tim The Toolman Taylor More Power Quote](/images/articles/tim-allen-tim-the-toolman-taylor-more-power-quote.webp)

---

## Remembering Earl Hindman (Wilson Wilson Jr.) — The Face Behind the Fence
For eight seasons, Tim Taylor solved every existential marriage and parenting dilemma by heading to the backyard wooden fence to seek the philosophical counsel of neighbor **Wilson Wilson Jr.** With his bucket hat, scholarly quotes from ancient philosophers, and mysterious hidden lower face, Earl Hindman turned Wilson into one of the most memorable characters in sitcom history.

Hindman was a respected character actor who spent 16 years portraying Detective Bob Reid on the daytime drama *Ryan's Hope*. On set, Hindman was famous for carrying a miniature picket fence on a stick during curtain calls so live studio audiences would never see his full face!

Tragically, on December 29, 2003, Earl Hindman passed away from lung cancer at age 61 in Stamford, Connecticut. When Tim Allen and Richard Karn reunited for their 2021 history series *Assembly Required*, they began the premiere with a touching tribute to Hindman, honoring him as the true wise heart of the show.

![Earl Hindman Wilson Wilsons Face Tribute](/images/articles/earl-hindman-wilson-wilsons-face-tribute.webp)

---

## The Taylor Boys: Where Are They in 2026?

### Jonathan Taylor Thomas (Randy Taylor) — The Teen Idol Who Walked Away
Throughout the mid-1990s, Jonathan Taylor Thomas (universally known as JTT) was the biggest teen idol on the planet. His face covered millions of bedroom posters in *Tiger Beat* and *BOP* magazine, and his vocal performance as young Simba in Disney's 1994 masterpiece *The Lion King* cemented his pop culture status.

However, Thomas possessed an intellectual curiosity that far exceeded Hollywood fame. At the start of Season 8 in 1998, JTT stunned executives by walking away from his multi-million-dollar role to focus on his academic education. Thomas attended Harvard University, studied at St. Andrews in Scotland, and graduated from Columbia University in 2010 with a degree in philosophy and history. Choosing a private, quiet life in Los Angeles, Thomas directed episodes of *Last Man Standing* and serves on the SAG-AFTRA National Board.

![Jonathan Taylor Thomas JTT 90s Teen Idol](/images/articles/jonathan-taylor-thomas-jtt-90s-teen-idol.webp)

### Zachery Ty Bryan (Brad Taylor) & Taran Noah Smith (Mark Taylor)
Zachery Ty Bryan played athletic eldest brother Brad Taylor. Bryan transitioned into producing, working on projects like *The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift*. In recent years, Bryan has faced widely publicized personal legal challenges and domestic controversies.

Taran Noah Smith portrayed youngest son Mark Taylor, who famously went through an emo-goth phase in later seasons. Smith walked away from acting immediately after *Home Improvement* concluded at age 16. He became an environmental pioneer, co-founding an organic vegan cheese manufacturer (*Playfood*) and later working as an installation engineer for submarine habitats with CommunitySubmersibles.

### Patricia Richardson (Jill Taylor) & Richard Karn (Al Borland)
Patricia Richardson received four Emmy nominations and two Golden Globe nominations for her sharp, grounded portrayal of Jill Taylor. Richardson has remained an active theater star on Broadway and television guest star (*The West Wing*, *NCIS*), serving on the national board of SAG-AFTRA.

Richard Karn became an instant fan favorite as Al Borland, the flannel-wearing master carpenter whose dry catchphrase *“I don’t think so, Tim”* prevented hundreds of studio catastrophes. Karn hosted game show *Family Feud* from 2002 to 2006 and reunited with Tim Allen in 2021 to co-host the tool competition series *Assembly Required*.

---

## Tool Time Secrets: Is Binford Tools a Real Company?

One of the most persistent questions fans have asked for over thirty years is whether **Binford Tools**—the fictional power tool manufacturer that sponsored *Tool Time*—was a real hardware corporation. From the heavy-duty Binford 6100 chainsaw to Binford pneumatic nail guns, Tim Taylor treated the brand like the Holy Grail of industrial engineering.

In reality, Binford Tools was entirely invented by series creators Matt Williams, Carmen Finestra, and David McFadzean. The name was chosen as a tribute to a real-life friend of the producers named John Binford. However, the fictional brand took on a massive real-world life of its own! 

During the show's peak, real tool manufacturers including DeWalt, Makita, and Milwaukee showered the production with thousands of dollars of free high-end equipment just to have their actual power tools painted with custom Binford stickers on television. Today, vintage Binford Tools t-shirts, metal toolboxes, and bumper stickers remain some of the most sought-after collector items among 1990s television enthusiasts.

title: The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air Cast Then and Now: Where Are They Today and Untold Reunion Secrets (2026 Update)
excerpt: From Will Smith's Oscar journey and James Avery's emotional legacy to Alfonso Ribeiro's Carlton dance and the historic 27-year Aunt Viv truce, explore Bel-Air in 2026.
content:
In September 1990, an infectious hip-hop beat and neon graffiti logo announced the arrival of *The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air* on NBC. Developed by music moguls Quincy Jones and Benny Medina, the show took a charismatic, Grammy-winning 21-year-old rapper from West Philadelphia who was facing financial ruin from unpaid IRS taxes—Will Smith—and placed him into a palatial Brentwood mansion alongside his wealthy, aristocratic relatives, the Banks family.

For six seasons and 148 episodes, *The Fresh Prince* was a cultural earthquake. It seamlessly blended laugh-out-loud physical comedy, innovative fourth-wall breaks, and vibrant 90s streetwear with deeply poignant explorations of race, class, paternal abandonment, and systemic privilege in America. 

Yet behind the iconic handshake routines with Jazz and Carlton’s preppy Tom Jones dances lay backstage tensions that fractured cast relationships for nearly three decades, as well as profound losses that reshaped the cast forever. In this 2026 deep-dive, we examine the untold true story of *The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air* and where its legendary stars are today.

![Fresh Prince of Bel-Air Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/fresh-prince-bel-air-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## James Avery (Uncle Phil) — The Heartbeat and Anchor of Bel-Air
No discussion of *The Fresh Prince* can begin without honoring the towering, magnetic presence of James Avery as Judge Philip Banks. Uncle Phil was the stern, booming moral titan of the Banks household—a distinguished civil rights veteran, brilliant jurist, and fiercely protective father who constantly threw Jazz out the front door, yet loved Will with unmatched depth.

A classically trained Shakespearean actor and decorated Vietnam War veteran, Avery served as a demanding yet loving mentor to a young, inexperienced Will Smith. Smith frequently recalled how Avery would lean in during dramatic scenes and whisper: *“Look at me. Use me. Don’t act, be.”* This dynamic culminated in Season 4's immortal episode *"Papa's Got a Brand New Excuse,"* where Will breaks down over his deadbeat father's abandonment (*"How come he don't want me, man?"*) and collapses into Uncle Phil’s unscripted, tearful embrace.

Tragically, on December 31, 2013, James Avery passed away at age 68 from complications following open-heart surgery in Glendale, California. His passing left an unfillable void in the hearts of his castmates. During the emotional 2020 HBO Max reunion, Will Smith wiped away tears as the cast watched a video montage of Avery, declaring: *“Every single time I walk into a room, I want to be what James Avery was to me.”*

![James Avery Uncle Phil Heartbreaking Tribute](/images/articles/james-avery-uncle-phil-heartbreaking-tribute.webp)

---

## Will Smith & The Banks Family: Where Are They in 2026?

### Will Smith (The Fresh Prince) — Global Icon, Oscar Winner & Executive Producer
Will Smith turned his breakout television role into one of the most unprecedented box office careers in cinematic history, reigning as Hollywood’s undisputed summer action king across blockbusters like *Bad Boys*, *Independence Day*, and *Men in Black*. In 2022, Smith captured the Academy Award for Best Actor for his tour-de-force performance as Richard Williams in *King Richard*.

In 2022, Smith executive produced Peacock’s dramatic reimagining, *Bel-Air*, which successfully adapted the original sitcom’s premise into a gritty, critically acclaimed hour-long drama running across multiple hit seasons. Rebounding from personal controversies with introspection, box office hits (*Bad Boys: Ride or Die*), and literary success with his bestselling 2021 memoir *Will*, Smith remains a towering titan of entertainment in 2026.

![Will Smith Fresh Prince How Come He Dont Want Me Quote](/images/articles/will-smith-fresh-prince-how-come-he-dont-want-me-quote.webp)

### Alfonso Ribeiro (Carlton Banks) — The Dance That Conquered Pop Culture
With his preppy pastel sweaters tied around his neck and conservative political aspirations, Carlton Banks was the ultimate comedic foil to Will’s streetwise cool. But it was Alfonso Ribeiro’s legendary *“Carlton Dance”*—set to Tom Jones’ *“It’s Not Unusual”*—that etched Carlton into the immortal pantheon of 90s television. Ribeiro revealed he created the dance by mashing up Courteney Cox dancing in Bruce Springsteen’s *“Dancing in the Dark”* video with Eddie Murphy’s *“white man dance”* routine!

A seasoned Broadway veteran and tap prodigy, Ribeiro won Season 19 of *Dancing with the Stars* in 2014 before taking over from Tom Bergeron as the beloved host of ABC’s *America’s Funniest Home Videos* in 2015. Today in 2026, Ribeiro is also the co-host of *Dancing with the Stars*, cementing his status as one of America's premier prime-time television personalities.

![Alfonso Ribeiro Carlton Banks The Carlton Dance](/images/articles/alfonso-ribeiro-carlton-banks-the-carlton-dance.webp)

### The 27-Year Aunt Viv Feud: Janet Hubert vs Daphne Maxwell Reid
For the first three seasons, Janet Hubert brought commanding elegance, vocal brilliance, and world-class Juilliard dance training to the role of Vivian Banks. Her electrifying Season 3 dance studio audition to *“Everybody Dance Now”* remains one of the most stunning physical sequences in sitcom history.

However, behind the scenes, intense creative clashes between Hubert and a young, headstrong Will Smith led to Hubert’s controversial departure in 1993, sparking a bitter 27-year public feud. Daphne Maxwell Reid was cast as Aunt Viv for Seasons 4 through 6, bringing a softer, warmly maternal energy to the character.

In November 2020, during the 30th Anniversary HBO Max Reunion, Will Smith and Janet Hubert sat down for an unprecedented, raw, and tearful reconciliation. Hubert bravely detailed how an abusive marriage, postpartum depression, and Hollywood blacklisting had devastated her life following her firing. Smith apologized deeply for his youthful lack of empathy, saying: *“I see your brilliance now. I am so sorry for the pain I caused you.”* Today, Hubert has enjoyed a triumphant career renaissance, earning an Emmy nomination for *Pose* and appearing in hit series like *Sweet Magnolias*.

![Janet Hubert Original Aunt Viv Reunion Then and Now](/images/articles/janet-hubert-original-aunt-viv-reunion-then-and-now.webp)

### Karyn Parsons (Hilary Banks) & Tatyana Ali (Ashley Banks)
As the spoiled, fashion-obsessed eldest daughter Hilary Banks, Karyn Parsons delivered hilarious, pitch-perfect deadpan comedy. Today, Parsons has transitioned into a celebrated author and cultural philanthropist, founding the non-profit *Sweet Blackberry* to produce animated films and books teaching children about unsung Black historical heroes.

Tatyana Ali grew up on screen as youngest sister Ashley Banks, blossoming into an accomplished singer with hit Billboard singles (*“Daydreamin’”*). Ali graduated from Harvard University in 2002 with a degree in Afro-American Studies and Government. In 2026, Ali is an outspoken civil rights advocate, mother of two, and celebrated actress who made a touching guest appearance as Mrs. Hughes in Peacock’s *Bel-Air* reboot!

![Karyn Parsons Hilary Banks Then and Now](/images/articles/karyn-parsons-hilary-banks-then-and-now.webp)

### Joseph Marcell (Geoffrey the Butler) & DJ Jazzy Jeff (Jazz)
English classical actor Joseph Marcell stole every scene as Geoffrey Butler, the sharply sarcastic British butler whose deadpan one-liners brought down the house. Marcell remains an acclaimed Shakespearean stage actor with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the Globe Theatre in London.

Meanwhile, Jeffrey Townes (DJ Jazzy Jeff)—Smith’s real-life hip-hop partner—was famous for being tossed out of the mansion by Uncle Phil (the exact same filmed clip was reused in dozens of episodes to save money!). Today, DJ Jazzy Jeff is revered worldwide as a pioneering turntablist legend, touring internationally and collaborating on groundbreaking musical projects.

![Joseph Marcell Geoffrey Butler Quote](/images/articles/joseph-marcell-geoffrey-butler-quote.webp)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why did Uncle Phil throw Jazz out in the exact same shirt every time?
Executive producers wanted to include the running visual gag of Uncle Phil physically tossing Jazz onto the front driveway. However, filming a live stunt on location in Brentwood was prohibitively expensive. To save production costs, producers filmed DJ Jazzy Jeff getting tossed onto the driveway once during Season 1, and subsequently required him to wear that exact same Hawaiian shirt in every episode where he was slated to get thrown out!

### Was Will Smith’s emotional father scene unscripted?
While the script for the Season 4 episode *"Papa's Got a Brand New Excuse"* always intended for Will's deadbeat father Lou to leave again, Will Smith's visceral, weeping breakdown at the end was entirely real. James Avery was so profoundly moved by Smith's acting breakthroughs that he wrapped Smith in an unscripted bear hug, whispering in his ear: *"That’s f***ing acting right there."*

### How did Will Smith and Janet Hubert finally resolve their 27-year feud?
For 27 years, Hubert and Smith traded bitter barbs in interviews. In 2020, ahead of the 30th anniversary reunion on HBO Max, Smith reached out to Hubert directly. During a two-hour private camera session, both shared tears, acknowledged past trauma, and apologized unconditionally. Their reconciliation is widely considered one of the most healing moments in television history.

### Is the real Bel-Air mansion located in Bel-Air?
No! The magnificent white mansion facade used for the establishing shots is actually located at 251 North Bristol Avenue in the neighboring upscale community of **Brentwood**, Los Angeles, not Bel-Air. In 2020, Will Smith partnered with Airbnb to allow lucky fans to stay inside the historic estate for a nostalgic weekend!

### Where can you stream every season of The Fresh Prince in 2026?
All six seasons of *The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air* (148 episodes) and the 2020 Reunion Special are streaming in remastered 1080p HD on Max and Hulu. The dramatic reboot *Bel-Air* streams exclusively on Peacock.

title: Boy Meets World Cast Then and Now: Mr. Turner's Vanishing, Feeny Lessons, and Where the Cast Is in 2026
excerpt: From William Daniels turning 98 and Danielle Fishel's directing career to Ben Savage's political run and the truth behind Mr. Turner's crash, explore Boy Meets World in 2026.
content:
Between 1993 and 2000, ABC’s TGIF lineup had plenty of high-energy sitcoms, but none navigated the raw, turbulent waters of adolescent coming-of-age with as much genuine heart, humor, and philosophical depth as *Boy Meets World*. Created by Michael Jacobs and April Kelly, the series began with an eleven-year-old sixth-grader named Cory Matthews (Ben Savage) grumbling about detention across his Philadelphia backyard fence with his teacher-neighbor Mr. Feeny (William Daniels).

Over seven seasons and 158 episodes, viewers watched Cory, his best friend Shawn Hunter (Rider Strong), and the love of his life Topanga Lawrence (Danielle Fishel) evolve from naive middle schoolers into mature college graduates. *Boy Meets World* stood out from its sitcom peers by tackling mature issues—trailer-park poverty, alcoholism, abusive parents, and existential grief—while preserving an unbreakable core of love and loyalty.

In this comprehensive 2026 retrospective, we examine the enduring legacy of *Boy Meets World*, investigate the infamous disappearance of beloved teacher Mr. Turner, celebrate the remarkable milestones of its cast, and reveal where the stars stand today.

![Boy Meets World Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/boy-meets-world-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## William Daniels (Mr. George Feeny) — American Television’s Greatest Teacher
Long before *Boy Meets World*, William Daniels was already an acting titan. He originated the role of John Adams in Broadway’s *1776*, voiced the iconic talking car K.I.T.T. on *Knight Rider*, and captured two Emmy Awards for his groundbreaking dramatic work as Dr. Mark Craig on NBC’s *St. Elsewhere*. 

Yet for millions of 90s kids, Daniels will forever be **Mr. George Feeny**—the neighbor, middle school teacher, high school principal, and college professor whose dignified moral guidance, uncompromising standards, and unconditional belief in his students made him the greatest teacher in television history. Daniels’ final scene in the empty classroom (*“Believe in yourselves. Dream. Try. Do good... I love you all. Class dismissed.”*) remains one of the most tearful, revered series finales of all time.

In 2025, William Daniels celebrated his monumental 98th birthday surrounded by his real-life wife of 74 years, Emmy-winning actress Bonnie Bartlett (who played Feeny's wife, Dean Bolander!), and his former TV students Ben Savage, Danielle Fishel, Rider Strong, and Will Friedle. Daniels’ sharp wit, loving wisdom, and dignified presence remain an inspiration to multiple generations.

![William Daniels Mr Feeny Feeny Call Tribute](/images/articles/william-daniels-mr-feeny-feeny-call-tribute.webp)

---

## The Core Trio: Where Are Cory, Topanga, and Shawn Today?

### Ben Savage (Cory Matthews) — From Everyman Teen to Congressional Candidate
As Cory Matthews, Ben Savage possessed an extraordinary everyman quality that allowed viewers of all ages to see themselves reflected in his neurotic anxieties, hair crises, and romantic devotion to Topanga. 

After *Boy Meets World* wrapped, Savage took a hiatus from acting to focus on higher education, graduating from Stanford University in 2004 with a degree in Political Science. He returned to television prominence in 2014, executive producing and starring in Disney Channel’s hit sequel *Girl Meets World*, portraying Cory as a loving father and history teacher in New York City. In recent years, Savage transitioned into civic public service: in 2022, he ran for West Hollywood City Council, and in 2024, he campaigned for the United States House of Representatives in California’s 30th Congressional District. In 2023, Savage married his longtime partner, Tessa Angermeier.

![Ben Savage Cory Matthews Then and Now](/images/articles/ben-savage-cory-matthews-then-and-now.webp)

### Danielle Fishel (Topanga Lawrence) — Director, Podcaster, and Cultural Icon
Topanga Lawrence was originally conceived as a one-off eccentric flower child for Episode 4 of Season 1. But Danielle Fishel’s magnetic screen charisma and undeniable chemistry with Ben Savage convinced producers to expand Topanga into the intellectual, emotional anchor of the entire series. 

Today in 2026, Danielle Fishel is one of the most respected, in-demand multi-cam television directors in Hollywood. After helming dozens of episodes of *Girl Meets World*, Fishel directed hit series including *Sydney to the Max*, *Raven’s Home*, and *The Villains of Valley View*. She is the host of the smash-hit retrospective podcast *Pod Meets World* alongside co-stars Rider Strong and Will Friedle, which consistently ranks among the top TV podcasts on Apple and Spotify. Fishel is married to writer Jensen Karp and is a proud mother of two young sons.

![Danielle Fishel Topanga Lawrence Then and Now](/images/articles/danielle-fishel-topanga-lawrence-then-and-now.webp)

### Rider Strong (Shawn Hunter) — The Poet, Director, and Columbia Scholar
As Cory’s street-smart, troubled best friend Shawn Hunter, Rider Strong delivered the most emotionally complex, heartbreaking performances on TGIF. Shawn’s painful struggles with parental abandonment, poverty, and searching for belonging resonated profoundly with millions of viewers.

Following the series, Strong pursued literary and academic pursuits, earning his Bachelor’s degree magna cum laude from Columbia University in 2004, followed by a Master of Fine Arts in English and creative writing. Strong has directed acclaimed indie films, written plays, and directed numerous episodes of *Girl Meets World*. On *Pod Meets World*, Strong’s thoughtful, philosophical analysis of 90s media has endeared him to a whole new generation of podcast listeners.

![Rider Strong Shawn Hunter Then and Now](/images/articles/rider-strong-shawn-hunter-then-and-now.webp)

---

## The Mystery of Mr. Turner: What Really Happened to Anthony Tyler Quinn?

In Season 2, the series introduced **Jonathan Turner** (Anthony Tyler Quinn), a cool, motorcycle-riding English teacher in a leather jacket who treated students with respect and took a homeless Shawn Hunter into his home as his legal guardian. Mr. Turner was a massive fan favorite.

However, in Season 4, Episode 21 (*“Cult Fiction”*), Mr. Turner suffers a catastrophic, near-fatal motorcycle crash. As he lies unconscious in an intensive care bed, Shawn falls to his knees and delivers an emotional, tear-filled prayer for Turner’s life.

And then... Mr. Turner simply vanished from the series! He never appeared in Seasons 5, 6, or 7, and the show offered zero explanation for his recovery or departure.

What really happened? Behind the scenes, the show was transitioning from high school to college, and network executives wanted to shift focus strictly to the core romantic couples. Quinn was placed on contract hold and eventually let go. However, 18 years later in 2015, justice was finally served: Michael Jacobs brought Anthony Tyler Quinn back for *Girl Meets World*, where it was revealed that Mr. Turner had survived the crash, married the nurse who saved his life, and had risen to become the Superintendent of New York City Public Schools! Today, Quinn holds a Master’s degree in Marriage and Family Therapy and continues to act.

![Anthony Tyler Quinn Mr Turner Motorcycle Crash](/images/articles/anthony-tyler-quinn-mr-turner-motorcycle-crash.webp)

### Will Friedle (Eric Matthews) — From “Feeny Call” to Voice Acting Legend
As Cory’s eccentric, wildly lovable older brother Eric Matthews, Will Friedle invented the famous high-pitched *“Feeny Call!”* (*“Fee-fee-fee-feeny!”*), which was entirely improvised on set. Friedle turned out to be one of the most prolific voice actors in modern animation history, voicing Terry McGinnis in *Batman Beyond*, Ron Stoppable in *Kim Possible*, Lion-O in *ThunderCats*, and Bumblebee in *Transformers Prime*. Friedle co-hosts *Pod Meets World* and *I Hear Voices*, remaining an indispensable staple of pop culture fandom.

![Will Friedle Eric Matthews Plays With Squirrels Quote](/images/articles/will-friedle-eric-matthews-plays-with-squirrels-quote.webp)

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Did Ben Savage and Danielle Fishel ever date in real life?
No. Despite having an on-screen romance that defined 1990s television, Ben Savage and Danielle Fishel never dated in real life. Fishel revealed that while they once went on a single dinner date to test if real-world chemistry existed, they both realized they were strictly like brother and sister. They have remained close lifelong friends for over thirty years.

### How did the “Feeny Call” originate?
The famous *“Fee-fee-feeee-ny!”* operatic call was never in any script! Will Friedle revealed on his podcast that during rehearsals for Season 4, he was looking for a comedic way to annoy William Daniels between takes. He improvised the high-pitched shriek, and the writers loved it so much they incorporated it into dozens of episodes.

### What is the story behind Trina McGee’s casting as Angela?
Trina McGee made television history in Season 5 when she was cast as Angela Moore, Shawn Hunter’s multi-season romantic partner. The relationship was groundbreaking as one of the first prominent, non-stereotypical interracial teenage romances on a major network primetime sitcom. content:
On October 4, 1990, visionary producer Aaron Spelling and creator Darren Star debuted an edgy primetime teen soap opera on FOX about twin siblings Brandon and Brenda Walsh moving from Minnesota to the affluent sunshine of Southern California. For ten seasons and 293 episodes, *Beverly Hills, 90210* was not merely a ratings powerhouse; it was a global pop-culture phenomenon that defined 1990s adolescent identity.

From the vibrant booths of the Peach Pit diner to the legendary love triangle of Brenda, Dylan, and Kelly (*"I choose me!"*), the series broke new ground by tackling teenage addiction, drunk driving, sexual consent, AIDS awareness, and eating disorders with unprecedented honesty.

Yet behind the glamorous convertibles and Pacific coast beach clubs, the real lives of the West Beverly High cast were punctuated by devastating tragedies, off-screen rivalries, and profound grief. In this comprehensive 2026 retrospective, we honor the beloved stars we have tragically lost and detail where the entire cast of *Beverly Hills, 90210* stands today.

![Beverly Hills 90210 Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/beverly-hills-90210-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## In Memoriam: The Heartbreaking Losses of Brenda and Dylan

### Shannen Doherty (Brenda Walsh) — The Rebel Who Fought with Unmatched Courage
As headstrong, passionate Brenda Walsh, Shannen Doherty was the electric spark plug of *Beverly Hills, 90210*. Her intense, magnetic romance with Dylan McKay and fiery clashes with father Jim Walsh captivated millions of viewers. While intense tabloid scrutiny and backstage friction led to her departure in Season 4, Doherty’s indelible talent established her as one of the defining screen presences of 90s television (later starring in Spelling's *Charmed*).

In 2015, Doherty revealed she had been diagnosed with breast cancer. Over nine grueling years, Doherty documented her treatments, surgeries, and metastasis to her brain and bones with astonishing vulnerability and bravery. Her podcast, *Let's Be Clear with Shannen Doherty*, became an international beacon of hope for cancer patients worldwide. 

Tragically, on July 13, 2024, Shannen Doherty passed away at age 53 in Malibu, California. Her death sent shockwaves through the global entertainment community. Co-star Jason Priestley mourned his on-screen twin, writing: *"Shocked and saddened by the passing of my friend Shannen. She was a force of nature and I will miss her."*

![Shannen Doherty Brenda Walsh Tribute](/images/articles/shannen-doherty-brenda-walsh-heartbreaking-tribute.webp)

### Luke Perry (Dylan McKay) — The James Dean of the 1990s
With his brooding brow, vintage Porsche 356 Speedster, sideburns, and tortured romantic soul, Luke Perry’s Dylan McKay was the ultimate 1990s teenage heartthrob. Mobs of thousands of screaming fans regularly forced mall appearances to shut down, causing police to declare local emergencies during the show's peak.

Perry possessed a rare, egoless kindness and humility that endeared him to everyone he worked with. He transitioned effortlessly into acclaimed character roles, starring as Fred Andrews—the deeply moral father figure—on The CW’s *Riverdale* and appearing in Quentin Tarantino’s *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood*.

Tragically, on February 27, 2019, Perry suffered a massive ischemic stroke at his home in Sherman Oaks. Despite intensive hospital care, Luke Perry passed away on March 4, 2019, at the young age of 52. His passing devastated the cast and millions of fans. During the 2019 meta-reboot *BH90210*, the cast dedicated the premiere to Perry, with Shannen Doherty joining the production specifically to honor his memory.

![Luke Perry Dylan McKay Tribute](/images/articles/luke-perry-dylan-mckay-heartbreaking-tribute.webp)

---

## West Beverly High: Where Is the Gang Today in 2026?

### Jason Priestley (Brandon Walsh) — The Director and TV Veteran
As Brandon Walsh, the upright high school journalist who drove his classic sedan "Mondale," Jason Priestley was the moral compass of Beverly Hills. Priestley also demonstrated immense talent behind the lens, directing 15 episodes of *90210*.

Following the series, Priestley survived a near-fatal 180 mph racecar crash at Kentucky Speedway in 2002, undergoing extensive reconstructive facial surgeries and physical therapy. A proud Canadian who was inducted into Canada’s Walk of Fame in 2016, Priestley has enjoyed a flourishing career as a leading director and star of long-running hits like *Call Me Fitz*, *Private Eyes*, and Global TV's crime dramedy *Wild Cards*.

![Jason Priestley Brandon Walsh Then and Now](/images/articles/jason-priestley-brandon-walsh-then-and-now.webp)

### Jennie Garth (Kelly Taylor) — The Peach Pit Glamour Girl
Jennie Garth's portrayal of Kelly Taylor took her character from a wealthy, insecure West Beverly party girl to a resilient, deeply empathetic young woman who survived cult manipulation, drug addiction, and romantic heartbreak. Garth was the only original cast member to appear in the first episode of *90210* in 1990 and recur in both the 2008 reboot and 2019 revival.

Today, Garth is a thriving media entrepreneur and author. Alongside co-star Tori Spelling, Garth hosts *9021OMG*, an award-winning retrospective podcast with millions of weekly downloads. Garth has starred in HGTV home renovation series *The Jennie Garth Project*, authored a memoir *Deep Thoughts From a Hollywood Blonde*, and launched her clothing and lifestyle brand *Me by Jennie Garth*.

![Jennie Garth Kelly Taylor Then and Now](/images/articles/jennie-garth-kelly-taylor-then-and-now.webp)

### Tori Spelling (Donna Martin) — From “Donna Martin Graduates!” to Reality Pioneer
Tori Spelling’s Donna Martin provided the show with sweet comedic innocence and cutting-edge 90s fashion. In Season 3, Donna was at the center of one of television's most iconic episodes, where the entire student body stages a walkout shouting *“DONNA MARTIN GRADUATES!”* after she is banned from graduation for drinking champagne at prom!

Spelling went on to become an architect of the celebrity reality television genre with hit shows like *Tori & Dean: Inn Love*. She is a *New York Times* bestselling author of six candid autobiographies. In recent years, Spelling has returned to podcasting, co-hosting *9021OMG* with Jennie Garth and launching her solo podcast *misSPELLING*.

![Tori Spelling Donna Martin Graduates Quote](/images/articles/tori-spelling-donna-martin-graduates-quote.webp)

### Brian Austin Green (David Silver) & Ian Ziering (Steve Sanders)
Starting as the dorky freshman DJ who desperately wanted to hang out with the cool seniors, Brian Austin Green’s David Silver underwent one of the show's most dramatic evolutions. Green transitioned into a prominent television star on *Terminator: The Sarah Connor Chronicles*, *Desperate Housewives*, and *Anger Management*. A father of five, Green is happily engaged to pro dancer Sharna Burgess, with whom he competed on *Dancing with the Stars*.

Ian Ziering brought roguish charm and athletic swagger to spoiled rich-kid Steve Sanders. Following the series, Ziering became an unexpected global cult phenomenon as chainsaw-wielding hero Fin Shepard in Syfy’s viral six-film *Sharknado* franchise! He is also a successful lifestyle and health entrepreneur.

### Gabrielle Carteris (Andrea Zuckerman) — The Union Leader
Cast at age 29 to play sixteen-year-old high school newspaper editor Andrea Zuckerman, Gabrielle Carteris kept her real age a strict secret during early auditions. Carteris transitioned into a formidable political leader in entertainment, serving as the President of SAG-AFTRA from 2016 to 2021, where she successfully led the union of 160,000 actors and media professionals through landmark labor contracts.

title: Family Matters Cast Then and Now: Where Are Steve Urkel and the Winslows Today? (2026 Update)
excerpt: From Jaleel White's Urkel phenomenon and Reginald VelJohnson's legacy to the mysterious vanishing of Judy Winslow, discover where the cast is in 2026.
content:
When *Family Matters* premiered on ABC in September 1989 as a modest spin-off of *Perfect Strangers*, it was conceived as a traditional blue-collar family sitcom centered around Chicago police officer Carl Winslow (Reginald VelJohnson) and his sharp-witted elevator operator wife Harriette (Jo Marie Payton). For eleven episodes, the series was a wholesome, grounded slice-of-life comedy.

Then, in Episode 12, a twelve-year-old guest actor named **Jaleel White** walked onto the set wearing high-waisted floodwater trousers, red suspenders, thick saddle shoes, and oversized black horn-rimmed spectacles, uttering five words in an ear-piercing nasal falsetto: *“Did I do that?!”*

What happened next was an unprecedented pop culture explosion. Steve Urkel transformed from a one-shot annoyance into a multi-million-dollar global merchandising juggernaut, inspiring Urkel-O's breakfast cereals, talking dolls, dance crazes, and Saturday morning cartoons. For nine seasons and 215 episodes, *Family Matters* was the second-longest-running non-animated sitcom with a predominantly Black cast in American history. 

In this comprehensive 2026 retrospective, we examine the true legacy of the Winslows, explore the backstage creative tensions that accompanied Urkel-mania, uncover the truth behind the show’s most infamous vanishing act, and reveal where the entire cast stands today.

![Family Matters Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/family-matters-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## Jaleel White (Steve Urkel & Stefan Urquelle) — The Reluctant Superstar
Jaleel White did not just play Steve Urkel; he carried the immense weight of an entire ABC primetime lineup on his pre-teen shoulders. White’s astonishing comedic range allowed him to portray multiple characters across the show’s run—including Urkel’s suave, smooth-talking DNA alter-ego **Stefan Urquelle**, his Southern belle cousin Myrtle Urkel, and various robotic clones. 

However, the relentless physical toll of pitching his vocal cords into a falsetto register for nine years caused severe strain, and the suffocating typecasting made it challenging for White to transition into mature adult roles after the show wrapped in 1998. 

Displaying remarkable business acumen, White graduated from UCLA’s School of Theater, Film and Television in 2001 with a degree in screenwriting. He voiced the iconic video game character Sonic the Hedgehog across three hit animated series, competed on *Dancing with the Stars*, appeared in films like *Hustle* alongside Adam Sandler, and launched *ItsPurpl*, a wildly successful upscale cannabis brand in collaboration with 710 Labs. In October 2024, White released his candid memoir, *Growing Up Urkel*, celebrating his legacy while sharing the complex realities of childhood fame. Today in 2026, White is happily married to tech executive Nicoletta Ruhl and remains a revered comedic trailblazer.

![Jaleel White Steve Urkel Did I Do That Quote](/images/articles/jaleel-white-steve-urkel-did-i-do-that-quote.webp)

---

## The Winslow Household: Where Are They Today?

### Reginald VelJohnson (Carl Winslow) — The Patriarch Who Embraced the Mayhem
Reginald VelJohnson brought warmth, formidable acting gravitas, and exquisite slow-burn comedic timing to Carl Winslow. Carl’s blood-pressure-spiking exasperation at Urkel blowing up his living room, wrecking his patrol car, or turning into a telekinetic fly was balanced by touching paternal moments where Carl served as Steve’s true father figure.

Already a cinematic legend for his beloved portrayal of LAPD Sgt. Al Powell in *Die Hard* (1988) and *Die Hard 2* (1990), VelJohnson has remained one of the hardest-working character actors in Hollywood. In 2024, at age 72, VelJohnson charmed millions as a fan-favorite contestant on Season 33 of *Dancing with the Stars*. He voices Principal Winslow on Amazon’s animated superhero smash *Invincible* and makes regular appearances in holiday films, proving his status as an eternal father figure to millions of 90s kids.

![Reginald VelJohnson Carl Winslow Then and Now](/images/articles/reginald-veljohnson-carl-winslow-then-and-now.webp)

### Jo Marie Payton (Harriette Winslow) — The Soul of the Series
Jo Marie Payton was the original foundation of *Family Matters*, having introduced Harriette Winslow on *Perfect Strangers*. Payton brought fierce matriarchal love, wisdom, and comedic groundedness to the household. 

As the series evolved from family-driven social issues into sci-fi Urkel plots featuring transformation chambers and time machines, Payton grew increasingly frustrated with the show's creative direction. She made the difficult decision to depart during Season 9, replaced by Judyann Elder for the remaining episodes. A celebrated vocal powerhouse, Payton has enjoyed over two decades of critical acclaim as the voice of Suga Mama on Disney’s *The Proud Family* and its hit reboot *The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder*. Today in 2026, Payton continues to perform live jazz and blues concerts worldwide.

![Jo Marie Payton Harriette Winslow Then and Now](/images/articles/jo-marie-payton-harriette-winslow-then-and-now.webp)

### Kellie Shanygne Williams (Laura Winslow) & Darius McCrary (Eddie Winslow)
As Laura Winslow, Kellie Shanygne Williams was the sharp, ambitious object of Steve Urkel’s relentless romantic obsession. For eight seasons, Laura rebuffed Steve's advances until the introduction of Stefan Urquelle gradually allowed Laura to appreciate Steve’s genuine loyalty and heart, culminating in their engagement in Season 9. After *Family Matters*, Williams chose to step away from Hollywood to raise her two children with husband Hannibal Jackson, founding the *Kellie Williams Program* in Washington, D.C., which mentors underprivileged youth in the fine arts.

Darius McCrary portrayed eldest son Eddie Winslow, navigating high school athletics, peer pressure, and classic 90s growing pains. Following the series, McCrary famously provided the voice of Autobot Jazz in Michael Bay’s 2007 blockbuster *Transformers*, starred on CBS's *The Young and the Restless*, and headlined urban drama *Monogamy*.

![Kellie Shanygne Williams Laura Winslow Then and Now](/images/articles/kellie-shanygne-williams-laura-winslow-then-and-now.webp)

### The Judy Winslow Mystery: Why Jaimee Foxworth Vanished
One of the most famous pieces of 1990s television trivia is the bizarre, abrupt disappearance of youngest daughter **Judy Winslow**, played by talented child actress Jaimee Foxworth. 

In Season 4, Episode 19 (*“Mama’s Wedding”*), nine-year-old Judy walks up the stairs of the Winslow home—and is literally never seen or mentioned again for the remaining five seasons of the show! Behind the scenes, the show had become entirely focused on Steve Urkel, whose escalating salary demands squeezed production budgets. Producers decided to eliminate Judy’s character without any on-screen explanation, birthing the television trope known as *“Chuck Cunningham Syndrome.”* 

Foxworth experienced painful personal struggles after being discarded by the production, battling depression and financial ruin. She bravely chronicled her recovery journey on VH1’s *Celebrity Rehab with Dr. Drew* in 2008. Today, Foxworth is a devoted mother and public advocate, frequently sharing her story to help protect child stars from industry exploitation.

![Jaimee Foxworth Judy Winslow Mystery](/images/articles/jaimee-foxworth-judy-winslow-mystery.webp)

### Rosetta LeNoire (Mother Winslow) & Telma Hopkins (Aunt Rachel)
Veteran Broadway pioneer Rosetta LeNoire portrayed the feisty, loving grandmother Estelle “Mother Winslow,” who always took Steve Urkel’s side against Carl’s grumbling. LeNoire was a civil rights champion who founded the AMAS Repertory Theatre; she passed away in 2002 at age 90, honored with the National Medal of Arts.

Telma Hopkins brought glamorous humor and vocal brilliance as Harriette's widowed sister Rachel Crawford, who opened Rachel's Place teen hangout after the original diner burned down. Already a musical legend with 1970s pop group Tony Orlando and Dawn, Hopkins enjoyed a flourishing post-TGIF career, starring in *Half & Half*, *The Parkers*, and *Dead to Me*.

![Steve Urkel Stefan Urquelle Alter Ego](/images/articles/steve-urkel-stefan-uelle-alter-ego.webp)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why did Judy Winslow randomly disappear from Family Matters?
Judy Winslow (Jaimee Foxworth) was written out of *Family Matters* at the end of Season 4 without any storyline explanation because the show had become completely focused on Steve Urkel. To accommodate Jaleel White’s substantial salary increases and budget constraints, executive producers determined Judy's character was expendable and deleted her from the family tree entirely!

### Did the Family Matters cast resent Jaleel White at first?
Yes. Both Jaleel White and Jo Marie Payton have openly acknowledged that when Urkel took over the show, the original cast felt blindsided and hurt. *Family Matters* was originally sold to Reginald VelJohnson and Jo Marie Payton as a mature ensemble family drama; suddenly having their storylines sidelined by a twelve-year-old guest star in suspenders created substantial initial backstage friction before the cast forged a loving, professional bond.

### How did Jaleel White come up with the voice for Steve Urkel?
During his audition in 1989, Jaleel White decided to speak in an extreme, high-pitched nasal register borrowed from a childhood impression of a dentist friend. He brought his father's thick dental glasses (without lenses) and borrowed his father's suspenders. The casting directors burst into uncontrollable laughter within thirty seconds, securing him the role on the spot.

### Where was the real Winslow house located?
The exterior house shown in establishing shots was located at 1516 West Wrightwood Avenue in Chicago’s Lincoln Park neighborhood. Despite passionate fan campaigns to save the historic 19th-century property, the original home was unfortunately demolished in 2017 to make way for modern luxury condominiums.

All nine seasons of *Family Matters* (215 episodes) are available for streaming in full high-definition on Max and Hulu.
