content:
For every American kid who grew up in the early 1990s, Saturday mornings did not truly begin until the high-energy electric guitar riffs and ringing school bell of NBC’s *Saved by the Bell* blasted through the living room CRT television. Debuting under its definitive title in 1989 after evolving from the short-lived Disney Channel series *Good Morning, Miss Bliss*, executive producer Peter Engel created a candy-colored, optimistic high school utopia at Palisades’ fictional Bayside High. 

With oversized neon locker hallways, the Max burger diner, cell phones the size of shoeboxes, and fourth-wall-breaking *“Time Out!”* freeze-frames, *Saved by the Bell* was a Saturday morning phenomenon that captured the imaginations of over 10 million weekly teen viewers across the globe.

Yet beneath the fluorescent sunshine of the Max, the true lives of Bayside's six core stars were marked by intense teenage dating triangles, high-stakes career reinventions, personal health battles, and the devastating, premature loss of one of television’s most iconic comedic sidekicks. In this 2026 retrospective, we journey back to the halls of Bayside High to see where Zack, Kelly, Slater, Jessie, Lisa, and Screech are today.

![Saved by the Bell Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/saved-by-the-bell-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## The Heartbreaking Passing of Dustin Diamond (Screech Powers)

No single character was more synonymous with *Saved by the Bell* than Samuel “Screech” Powers, portrayed with rubber-faced physical hilarity and unmatched vocal flexibility by child prodigy Dustin Diamond. Cast when he was just eleven years old—three years younger than the rest of the teenage cast—Diamond brought Screech to life through wild patterned shirts, his homemade robot companion Kevin, science fair mishaps, and an enduring, hopelessly unrequited crush on fashionista Lisa Turtle.

Remarkably, Diamond was the only original cast member to appear in every single incarnation of the franchise, spanning *Good Morning, Miss Bliss*, all four seasons of *Saved by the Bell*, *The College Years*, two television movies, and all seven seasons of *The New Class*, tallying an astounding 240+ episodes.

However, life after Bayside proved profoundly difficult for Diamond. Struggling to break free from the suffocating typecasting of Screech, he faced financial bankruptcies, legal run-ins, and public alienation from his former co-stars following the publication of a ghostwritten 2009 tell-all book, *Behind the Bell*, which he later publicly retracted and apologized for.

In January 2021, Diamond was hospitalized in Florida after feeling persistent physical pain; doctors delivered a devastating diagnosis of Stage 4 small-cell lung carcinoma that had rapidly metastasized. Just three weeks later, on February 1, 2021, Dustin Diamond passed away at the tragic age of 44. Co-stars Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez spoke with Diamond shortly before his death, with Lopez remembering him as *“a true comedic genius whose goofy warmth brightened our childhoods.”* When the Peacock sequel series aired its second season, the cast dedicated a tearful, poignant memorial episode to Screech at The Max, ensuring his place in television history would never be forgotten.

![Dustin Diamond Screech Powers Tribute](/images/articles/dustin-diamond-screech-powers-tribute.webp)

---

## The Bayside Core: Where Are They in 2026?

### Mark-Paul Gosselaar (Zack Morris) — From Teen Schemer to Acclaimed Dramatic Star
With his peroxide-blonde hair, oversized brick cell phone, and undeniable charm, Zack Morris was the ultimate high school schemer who could talk his way out of detention with Principal Belding and freeze live television action with a snap of his fingers. Naturally brunette, Gosselaar had his hair chemically bleached every two weeks for five straight years to maintain Zack’s golden California aesthetic.

Proving his skeptics wrong, Gosselaar engineered one of the most successful transitions from teen idol to respected dramatic actor in Hollywood history. He spent four seasons playing Detective John Clark Jr. on ABC’s gritty police procedural *NYPD Blue*, starred in TNT’s legal dramedy *Franklin & Bash*, earned rave reviews for the critically acclaimed baseball drama *Pitch*, and currently stars in NBC’s hit missing-persons thriller *Found*. In 2020, Gosselaar reprised Zack Morris in the Peacock reboot, where the older, self-absorbed Zack had somehow maneuvered his way into becoming the Governor of California!

![Mark-Paul Gosselaar Zack Morris Time Out](/images/articles/mark-paul-gosselaar-zack-morris-time-out.webp)

### Mario Lopez (A.C. Slater) — The Dimpled Jock Turned Entertainment Mogul
Albert Clifford “A.C.” Slater strutted into Bayside High in his tight wrestling singlets and backwards caps, calling Zack *“Preppy”* and immediately engaging in an epic battle for Kelly Kapowski’s heart before becoming Zack’s truest brother. 

Today, Mario Lopez is one of the most recognizable, prolific television hosts in American broadcasting. After finishing as runner-up on *Dancing with the Stars* in 2006, Lopez cemented his broadcast career hosting *Extra*, *The X Factor*, and *Access Hollywood*. An avid Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu practitioner who earned his black belt, Lopez is also a bestselling author and devoted father of three with wife Courtney Mazza. In the 2020 Peacock reboot, Lopez reprised Slater as Bayside's beloved physical education teacher and athletic director.

![Mario Lopez AC Slater Then and Now](/images/articles/mario-lopez-ac-slater-then-and-now.webp)

### Tiffani Thiessen (Kelly Kapowski) — America’s Forever High School Sweetheart
As head cheerleader, volleyball captain, and homecoming queen Kelly Kapowski, Tiffani Thiessen was the quintessential 1990s dream crush for an entire generation. From her high-waisted acid-washed jeans to her off-the-shoulder Bayside sweatshirts, Thiessen’s Kelly set nationwide fashion trends.

Immediately after *Saved by the Bell* wrapped, Thiessen shattered her squeaky-clean image by joining the cast of FOX’s primetime juggernaut *Beverly Hills, 90210* as scheming vixen Valerie Malone. She went on to star in USA Network’s beloved series *White Collar* for six seasons. Over the past decade, Thiessen has channeled her passion for entertaining into the culinary world, hosting *Dinner at Tiffani’s* on the Cooking Channel, authoring bestselling cookbooks *Pull Up a Chair* and *Here We Go Again*, and hosting comedy clip show *Deliciousness* on MTV.

![Tiffani Thiessen Kelly Kapowski Then and Now](/images/articles/tiffani-thiessen-kelly-kapowski-then-and-now.webp)

### Elizabeth Berkley (Jessie Spano) — From “I’m So Excited!” to Teen Empowerment Icon
As high-achieving feminist valedictorian Jessica “Jessie” Spano, Elizabeth Berkley brought passionate social consciousness and academic ambition to Saturday mornings. Her performance in the legendary 1990 episode where an over-caffeinated Jessie collapses while singing The Pointer Sisters’ *“I’m So Excited!”* remains one of the most viral, iconic scenes in the history of youth television.

Following the series, Berkley took a bold leap into feature films, starring in Paul Verhoeven’s controversial 1995 cult classic *Showgirls*. While initially polarizing, the film has since been reclaimed as a camp masterpiece, and Berkley received widespread critical redemption on Broadway and television (including *The L Word* and *CSI: Miami*). Berkley founded *Ask-Elizabeth*, an acclaimed nationwide adolescent self-esteem program and bestselling book that has empowered hundreds of thousands of teenage girls across American schools. She returned as an executive producer and star of the 2020 *Saved by the Bell* revival, portraying Bayside's high school guidance counselor.

![Elizabeth Berkley Jessie Spano So Excited Quote Card](/images/articles/elizabeth-berkley-jessie-spano-so-excited-quote.webp)

### Lark Voorhies (Lisa Turtle) — Bayside’s Fashion Pioneer
Lark Voorhies was pure elegance and comedic timing as Lisa Turtle, the wealthy, high-fashion trendsetter who relentlessly shut down Screech’s corny pickup lines while maintaining a fiercely loyal bond with Kelly and Jessie. Voorhies won two Young Artist Awards for her magnetic performance.

Following *Saved by the Bell*, Voorhies enjoyed steady roles on daytime soap operas *Days of Our Lives* and *The Bold and the Beautiful*. In recent years, Voorhies stepped away from the spotlight to manage schizoaffective disorder, supported by her loving mother. After fans campaigned for her inclusion, Voorhies made a celebrated, radiant guest return in the Peacock revival series as a world-famous international fashion designer.

![Lark Voorhies Lisa Turtle Then and Now](/images/articles/lark-voorhies-lisa-turtle-then-and-now.webp)

### Dennis Haskins (Principal Richard Belding) — “Hey, Hey, Hey!”
No discussion of Bayside High is complete without Dennis Haskins’ unforgettable portrayal of Principal Richard Belding. Haskins brought genuine warmth and comic exasperation to Belding’s constant battle to keep Zack Morris from running unauthorized casino operations and radio stations in the locker rooms. In 2026, Haskins remains a beloved fixture at 90s fan conventions, frequently visiting college campuses to lead alumni in the iconic Bayside school fight song.

![Dennis Haskins Mr Belding Hey Hey Quote](/images/articles/dennis-haskins-mr-belding-hey-hey-quote.webp)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Did the Saved by the Bell cast date in real life?
Yes! Producer Peter Engel revealed that during the high school years of filming, virtually all the core cast members dated one another off-screen. Mark-Paul Gosselaar briefly dated Lark Voorhies for several years, had an off-screen relationship with Tiffani Thiessen, and later dated Elizabeth Berkley. Mario Lopez and Tiffani Thiessen also dated during the later seasons of the series.

### What happened to Dustin Diamond’s character Screech in the reboot?
In Season 2 of the 2020 Peacock sequel series, the writers poignantly revealed that Screech was living on the International Space Station with his robot Kevin. Following Dustin Diamond's real-life passing in February 2021, the cast gathered at The Max in an emotional tribute scene to share fond memories of Screech over burgers, officially dedicating the episode to Diamond.

### Why was Tori Scott (Leanna Creel) on the show without Kelly and Jessie?
When NBC originally ordered additional episodes for Season 4, Tiffani Thiessen and Elizabeth Berkley had already committed to other projects. The network hired Leanna Creel to play leather-jacket-wearing transfer student Tori Scott for a 10-episode block. In syndication, NBC aired the Tori episodes mixed together with the graduation episodes, creating the hilarious illusion that Kelly and Jessie randomly vanished and reappeared!

### Where was Bayside High filmed?
Despite being set in Palisades, California, *Saved by the Bell* was filmed on Stage 4 at Sunset Gower Studios in Hollywood. The exact same school hallway and classroom sets were later repurposed for numerous other teen sitcoms, including *Hang Time* and *City Guys*.

### Where can you stream Saved by the Bell in 2026?
All four seasons of the original *Saved by the Bell*, along with *The College Years* and the 2020 revival, are available for streaming on Peacock and Hulu in remastered digital formats.

title: Friends Cast Then and Now: Matthew Perry Tribute, Untold Secrets, and Where the Six Are in 2026
excerpt: From Matthew Perry's heartbreaking loss and Jennifer Aniston's mogul status to $1M salaries and Central Perk secrets, discover where the Friends cast is in 2026.
content:
On September 22, 1994, NBC unveiled a new comedy about six twenty-somethings living in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village, drinking coffee on an oversized orange velvet couch at Central Perk. Created by David Crane and Marta Kauffman, *Friends* did not merely capture an audience; it redefined television history, reigning as the undisputed sovereign of NBC’s legendary “Must-See TV” Thursday night lineup.

For ten seasons and 236 episodes, Rachel Green, Monica Geller, Phoebe Buffay, Joey Tribbiani, Chandler Bing, and Ross Geller became surrogate family members to an estimated 52 million American viewers during its 2004 series finale. The show set global fashion trends (the ubiquitous “Rachel” haircut), popularized pop-culture phrases (*“Could I BE any more...?”*, *“How you doin’?”*, *“WE WERE ON A BREAK!”*), and proved that genuine ensemble solidarity could force network executives to pay each actor an unprecedented $1 million per episode.

Yet beneath the sparkling comedic banter and Central Perk coffee cups lay private battles with addiction, tragic premature losses, and complex post-sitcom transformations. In this comprehensive 2026 retrospective, we honor the beloved stars we have lost, celebrate the enduring triumphs of the six, and detail where the entire cast of *Friends* stands today.

![Friends Cast Then and Now 2026](/images/articles/friends-cast-then-and-now-2026.webp)

---

## Matthew Perry (Chandler Bing) — The King of Sarcasm and a Heart of Gold
No single character delivered more unforgettable comedic timing, self-deprecating wit, and emotional vulnerability than Chandler Bing, brought to life with genius improvisation by **Matthew Perry**. Perry’s idiosyncratic cadences transformed simple lines into immortal catchphrases, and his romantic evolution from neurotic commitment-phobe to Monica Geller’s devoted husband provided *Friends* with its most touching emotional anchor.

Yet behind the dazzling laughter, Perry was fighting a desperate, harrowing battle with severe drug and alcohol addiction throughout the show's height, at one point consuming 55 Vicodin pills a day. In November 2022, Perry published his deeply candid, bestselling memoir, *Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing*, recounting his dozens of detox attempts, multiple life-saving surgeries, and his ultimate mission: *“When I die, I want helping people with addiction to be the first thing that's mentioned, not Friends.”*

Tragically, on October 28, 2023, the world was devastated when Matthew Perry was found deceased in the hot tub of his Pacific Palisades home at age 54. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner determined his death was caused by the acute effects of ketamine, leading to federal criminal investigations. The surviving five cast members released an agonizing joint statement: *“We are all so utterly devastated by the loss of Matthew. We were more than just cast mates. We are a family.”* In 2026, Perry’s enduring legacy of kindness lives on through the Matthew Perry Foundation, providing vital resources and hope to those battling addiction.

![Matthew Perry Chandler Bing Tribute](/images/articles/matthew-perry-chandler-bing-could-i-be-any-more-tribute.webp)

---

## The Central Perk Six: Where Are They in 2026?

### Jennifer Aniston (Rachel Green) — Hollywood’s Ultimate Mogul
When Jennifer Aniston burst onto screens in a rain-soaked wedding dress in 1994, she initiated a worldwide cultural phenomenon. Her hairstyle—dubbed “The Rachel”—was copied by an estimated 11 million women worldwide, and her multi-season *“Will they or won’t they?”* romance with Ross Geller captivated the globe.

Aniston leveraged *Friends* into an untouchable A-list Hollywood career, headlining hit films like *Marley & Me*, *We’re the Millers*, and *Bruce Almighty*. Since 2019, Aniston has produced and starred in Apple TV+’s flagship drama *The Morning Show* as news anchor Alex Levy, earning multiple Emmy and SAG Award nominations. In 2021, she launched *LolaVie*, an award-winning premium haircare brand that has become a retail juggernaut. Today in 2026, Aniston stands as one of the most powerful, respected producer-actresses in the entertainment industry.

![Jennifer Aniston Rachel Green The Rachel Haircut Then and Now](/images/articles/jennifer-aniston-rachel-green-the-rachel-haircut-then-and-now.webp)

### Courteney Cox (Monica Geller) — Scream Queen, Director & Homecourt Founder
As the hyper-competitive, obsessively clean host of Apartment 20, Courteney Cox was the maternal glue holding the group together. Her famous exclamation *“I KNOW!”* and her romance with Chandler Bing provided the emotional foundation of the show’s later seasons.

During and after *Friends*, Cox established horror cinema immortality as intrepid reporter Gale Weathers in the iconic *Scream* franchise—the only actor to appear in all seven installments of the franchise! She starred in six seasons of ABC’s *Cougar Town* (which she also directed), headlined horror-comedy *Shining Vale*, and launched *Homecourt*, an acclaimed luxury home fragrance and lifestyle brand. Cox remains exceptionally close with Aniston and Kudrow, frequently sharing hilarious reunion videos on social media.

![Courteney Cox Monica Geller I Know Quote](/images/articles/courteney-cox-monica-geller-i-know-quote.webp)

### Lisa Kudrow (Phoebe Buffay) — The Creative Genius Behind “Smelly Cat”
Lisa Kudrow brought eccentric brilliance, acoustic guitar anthems (*“Smelly Cat”*), and unexpected street wisdom to Phoebe Buffay (and her mischievous twin sister Ursula). Kudrow was the first *Friends* cast member to win an Emmy Award for her performance in 1998.

Kudrow established herself as one of Hollywood’s sharpest comedic minds, co-creating and starring in the groundbreaking HBO comedy *The Comeback* (which earned her two additional Emmy nominations) and pioneering digital series *Web Therapy*. In recent years, Kudrow has starred in Taika Waititi’s *Time Bandits* on Apple TV+ and comedy hit *Palm Royale*. A Vassar College biology graduate who initially conducted headache research with her physician father, Kudrow remains one of television’s most intellectually formidable stars.

![Lisa Kudrow Phoebe Buffay Smelly Cat Quote](/images/articles/lisa-kudrow-phoebe-buffay-smelly-cat-quote.webp)

### Matt LeBlanc (Joey Tribbiani) — “How You Doin’?”
Matt LeBlanc’s portrayal of dim-witted, big-hearted Italian-American actor Joey Tribbiani gave television some of its greatest punchlines (*“Joey doesn’t share food!”*). LeBlanc’s smooth pickup line *“How you doin’?”* became a global phenomenon.

Following the two-season spin-off *Joey*, LeBlanc delivered a career-defining satirical performance playing an exaggerated version of himself in Showtime’s *Episodes*, which earned him four Emmy nominations and a Golden Globe Award. He co-hosted BBC’s international phenomenon *Top Gear* for three seasons and starred in CBS sitcom *Man with a Plan*. Today in 2026, LeBlanc enjoys a quiet life in Southern California, passionately restoring classic motorcycles and vintage automobiles.

![Matt LeBlanc Joey Tribbiani How You Doin Quote](/images/articles/matt-leblanc-joey-tribbiani-how-you-doin-quote.webp)

### David Schwimmer (Ross Geller) — Theater Director and Dramatic Powerhouse
David Schwimmer’s physical comedy as paleontologist Ross Geller—from the leather pants disaster to teeth-whitening mishaps and shouting *“PIVOT!”* on the staircase—was hailed by critics as television clowning at its highest level. Schwimmer also directed ten memorable episodes of the series.

A co-founder of Chicago’s acclaimed Lookingglass Theatre Company, Schwimmer has dedicated much of his career to live stage directing and dramatic roles. In 2016, Schwimmer received an Emmy nomination for his chilling, nuanced portrayal of defense attorney Robert Kardashian in FX’s *The People v. O.J. Simpson: American Crime Story*. He starred in Apple TV+’s *Extrapolations* and Disney+’s *Goosebumps*, continuing to work as a prolific stage and screen actor.

![David Schwimmer Ross Geller We Were On a Break Quote](/images/articles/david-schwimmer-ross-geller-we-were-on-a-break-quote.webp)

---

## Remembering James Michael Tyler (Gunther)

Beyond the six leads, no guest character was more beloved than **Gunther**, the bleached-blonde Central Perk barista portrayed with dry, deadpan brilliance by James Michael Tyler. Appearing in 148 episodes, Gunther harbored an enduring, unrequited love for Rachel Green.

Tragically, on October 24, 2021, James Michael Tyler passed away at his home in Los Angeles at age 59 following a courageous battle with Stage 4 prostate cancer. Tyler appeared via Zoom during the 2021 HBO Max reunion to express his lifelong gratitude to the cast. Co-star Jennifer Aniston honored him warmly: *“Friends would not have been the same without you. Thank you for the laughter you brought to the show and to all of our lives.”*

The central debate of 1990s television! James Michael Tyler was originally hired as an uncredited extra for the Central Perk coffee shop background simply because he was the only background actor on set who actually knew how to operate a commercial espresso machine! No! Despite the opening credits portraying the cast splashing in a fountain in front of New York brownstones, the scene was filmed at 4:00 AM on the Warner Bros. Ranch in Burbank, California, in a fountain located on French Street!
